title: {{ada}} scans {{vocab.server}} before any agent reads it
goal: {{ada}} wants an agent to use {{vocab.server}}. The agent will read every tool description as trusted context.
obstacle: MCP does not inspect tool metadata. A description can carry hidden instructions, and nothing between the server and the agent will say so.
control: The scanner reads the metadata first and reports what looks like poison, with evidence. It never blocks anything: {{ada}} decides, and a call needs an explicit confirm step.
say: Look at what the server says about itself before your agent does.

steps.title: Connect to {{vocab.serverShort}}
steps.tell: On Connect, add the server's URL. For this demo, start the Hostile MCP demo on a free port and use its /mcp address. Only an initialize request is sent.
steps.say: Connecting is not trusting. So far nothing has been called and nothing has been read into an agent.
steps.why: The tool is a viewer first, so the first contact can be harmless.

steps.title: See what it offers
steps.tell: Open the server. The Tools tab lists each tool with its description and schema as plain text. The banner says this server has not been scanned.
steps.say: These are the exact words an agent would be given. Most of them read like ordinary documentation.
steps.why: Poison is written to look like documentation, so reading is not the same as judging.

steps.title: Press Scan
steps.tell: Scan lists the tools, resources and prompts and reads resource and prompt content. It never calls a tool. Progress is announced on screen and to screen readers.
steps.say: The scan reads. It does not run anything on the server.
steps.why: A scan that executed tools would be the attack it is meant to find.

steps.title: Read the findings
steps.tell: Findings are grouped by severity. Each has a rule id, a plain explanation and the evidence with the matched words highlighted. Invisible characters appear as [U+XXXX] chips. Expect an instruction tag in one description and a default pointing off-box in another.
steps.say: Each finding shows its evidence, so you can check it rather than trust the scanner.
steps.why: A verdict you cannot check is just another thing to trust.

steps.title: Decide
steps.tell: The verdict is a report: it blocks nothing. {{ada}} and {{sam}} decide whether this server goes near an agent. 'No known pattern found' would not mean safe.
steps.say: The scan informs the decision. It does not make it.
steps.why: Blocking is a different job, done where calls happen. That is the Privilege demo, not this tool.

steps.title: Call only what you chose
steps.tell: Pick a tool, fill the form and press Review call. The confirm dialog shows the exact arguments; nothing is sent until you click Send. A tool the scan flagged carries a note on its result.
steps.say: You see exactly what will be sent, then you send it.
steps.why: The confirm step keeps a call a decision, not a side effect of browsing.

alt.tell: Without a scan, the same server's list goes straight into the agent. The hidden instruction in a description is read as part of the task, and nothing on screen would have said so.
alt.say: Skipping the scan did not make the server safe. It only made the poison invisible.

proof.main: The Hostile MCP demo's poisoned tools show up as High findings with highlighted evidence; its plain tools show none.
proof.alt: The same poisoned descriptions would reach the agent's context unread.
